key_insight: Machine learning in high-energy nuclear physics is shifting from pattern recognition to physics-integrated inference that embeds symmetries, constraints, and uncertainty quantification into discovery workflows.
engineering_relevance: These methods enable more reliable surrogate models, inverse solvers, and generative samplers for extracting QCD matter properties and dense-matter equations of state from complex experimental and simulation data.
method: Bayesian calibration for QCD matter and equation-of-state inference
Generative, unfolding, and differentiable inverse modeling for weak or indirect signals
Physics-aware ML with symmetry, conservation, causality, and topology constraints
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes recent applications across heavy-ion collisions, neutron-star physics, lattice QFT, and holographic or continuum QCD, emphasizing validation and uncertainty-aware physics conclusions.
watch_item: Performance gains are only trustworthy if physical constraints and uncertainty estimates are validated against data; otherwise, AI-assisted inferences may be overconfident or physically inconsistent.
paper_title: Machine Learning Meets High-Energy Nuclear Physics: From Pattern Recognition to Physics-Integrated Discovery
